title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S is a smooth relative curve and ω (written \underline{ω}) is a line bundle, presumably Ω^1_{X/S} or a twist of it. P = ℙ(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) is the ℙ^1-bundle of 1-jets (principal parts) of ω. It carries the canonical section σ coming from the jet filtration. A 'projective connection' (projective structure) on X/S is encoded as a relative connection on P for which σ is nowhere stationary, i.e. an sl_2-oper in modern language.

Previous page: any other connection differs from a fixed D_0 by a 1-form ω_1, and the relevant quadratic invariant transforms by the Riccati/Schwarzian-type rule c_{D_0+ω_1} = c_{D_0} + 2D_0(ω_1) + ω_1^2. In a coordinate with D_0 = d and ω_1 = λ dt, regularity of 2λ' + λ^2 at a pole of λ forces λ = 2/t + O(t), with no constant term.

This page solves the global model case. Take f : X → E^1_S ⊂ ℙ^1_S, a map to the affine line with coordinate t. Let D_f be the projective connection pulled back by f. Horizontal sections of P for ∇_{D_f} correspond to connections D_f + λ dt with c unchanged, i.e. to solutions of the Riccati equation 2λ' + λ^2 = 0. Its solutions are λ = 0 and λ = 2/(t − a).

Grothendieck then gives the conceptual reason. D_f is the inverse image of the canonical projective connection of ℙ^1_S. That connection exists even though Ω^1_{ℙ^1_S/S} (degree −2) admits no globally defined connection. So the horizontal sections over X are obtained by pulling back the horizontal sections of ℙ(P^1_{ℙ^1_S/S}(ω)) over ℙ^1_S. Those are parametrised by the points a ∈ ℙ^1: λ = 2/(t−a), with a = ∞ giving λ = 0.

This matches the classical fact that the flat ℙ^1-bundle of the standard projective structure on ℙ^1 is ℙ^1 × ℙ^1, whose flat sections are the constant ones (the developing map is the identity). The page serves the programme of the next page: listing equivalent descriptions of projective structures on X/S, namely (a) the oper triple (P, σ, c), (b) a filtered sl_2-type Lie algebra with connection, (c) an extension of the order-3 jet isomorphism, and (d) a PGL_2-invariant third-order ODE.
errors: No mathematical error. The Riccati equation 2λ' + λ^2 = 0 has exactly the solutions λ = 2/(t−a) and λ = 0. This is consistent with the previous page's polar condition λ = 2/t + (order ≥ 1), with no constant term.
The transcription's '2λ^1 + λ^2 = 0' should read 2λ' + λ^2 = 0 (derivative).

ideas.what: Horizontal sections of the jet ℙ^1-bundle for a projective connection correspond to solutions of a Riccati equation 2λ' + λ^2 = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Riccati equation / Schwarzian transformation law for projective structures

ideas.what: The canonical projective connection on ℙ^1_S exists although Ω^1_{ℙ^1_S/S} has no global connection; projective structures pulled back along a map to ℙ^1 have flat sections pulled back from ℙ^1.
ideas.modern_name: Standard projective structure on ℙ^1; developing map; sl_2-oper on ℙ^1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; algebraic relative version in Deligne (LNM 163, 1970) and Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s)

ideas.what: Encoding projective connections as connections on ℙ(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) with a nonstationary canonical section, in a relative setting over a general base S.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Beilinson–Drinfeld (1993/2005); related: Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory (indigenous bundles); Gunning (indigenous bundles)

missed.claim: This page belongs to an unpublished algebraic, relative-to-S treatment of projective structures as connections on the jet ℙ^1-bundle with a nonstationary section, i.e. opers. This predates Beilinson–Drinfeld's terminology, in a file linked to Gauss–Manin and Cartier operations. The page itself only works out the routine flat-section computation for the model ℙ^1.
missed.quote: Comme D_f est l'image inv. de la conn. proj. canonique de ℙ^1_S — (qui existe bien qu'il n'y ait pas de connexion partout définie sur Ω^1_{ℙ^1_S/S} !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck working on oper-like structures over general bases, potentially in characteristic p given the Cartier context. This parallels the later dormant-oper/Mochizuki story. No new mathematical result appears on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is classical: the Riccati equation and the flat sections of the standard projective structure on ℙ^1. Interest is mainly historical, as part of an early relative oper-style framework developed on neighbouring pages.
transcription_corrections: '∇_{D_t}' in line 1 is likely '∇_{D_f}' (the projective connection defined by f).
'ℙ_{ℙ^1_S/S}' at the end presumably abbreviates ℙ(P^1_{ℙ^1_S/S}(ω)), the jet ℙ^1-bundle over ℙ^1_S.
The marginal addition reads roughly 'la conn. déf. par f : X → E^1_S ⊂ ℙ^1_S', with E^1_S the affine line.
